label: dense near-always-on feature (strongest in copy phase when outputting s/z/n/f/r/x/w)
explanation: Active on 89% of all steps and on every sequence, so there is no selective binary trigger. Rate is lowest at t=0 (50%) and t=1 (73%) and roughly 90-97% everywhere else; t >= 2 gives dev F1 0.92 vs 0.94 for the trivial always-true predicate. Magnitude has structure: the top activations are copy-phase steps whose output token is s (also z, n, f, r, x, w). Copy steps with out_tok in that set are 100% active and carry about 25% of activation mass, but that set covers only 13% of active steps. Lowest-quartile activity is spread weakly across ordinary original-phase and copy steps. Input token, L, digits and repeats have little effect.
